name: murphy-filesystem-extra
description: Extra vetted file-permission and legacy-tool checks (CIS Linux 6.1 / 2.3). Absent paths SKIP or PASS, never false-fail.

rules.title: /etc/shadow- backup is root-only
rules.rationale: The shadow backup holds the same password hashes as the live file; a loose mode leaks them for offline cracking.

rules.title: /etc/gshadow- backup is root-only
rules.rationale: Group password backup — same leak risk as shadow-.

rules.title: /etc/passwd- backup not world/group writable
rules.rationale: A writable passwd backup can be swapped in to seed rogue accounts.

rules.title: /etc/group- backup not world/group writable
rules.rationale: A writable group backup can be used to grant group membership (e.g. wheel/sudo).

rules.title: sshd_config not world/group writable
rules.rationale: A writable sshd_config lets a local user weaken SSH (re-enable root/password login) before the next reload.

rules.title: GRUB config is root-only
rules.rationale: A readable/writable grub.cfg leaks boot parameters and can hide a password hash or be edited to weaken boot.
rules.fix: chmod 600 /boot/grub/grub.cfg (path SKIPs if your bootloader differs)

rules.title: /etc/cron.d is root-only
rules.rationale: Anyone who can write into a cron directory schedules code as root.

rules.title: rlogin client absent
rules.rationale: rlogin trusts host-based auth and speaks cleartext — a lateral-movement gift.

rules.title: rcp client absent
rules.rationale: rcp is the cleartext cousin of scp; its presence invites insecure copies.

rules.title: NIS client (ypbind) absent
rules.rationale: NIS/yp is an obsolete, unauthenticated directory service — a well-known soft target.
rules.fix: Remove NIS; use LDAP/SSSD or local accounts.

rules.title: TFTP client absent
rules.rationale: TFTP has no authentication and is a common exfil/staging tool once a box is popped.
rules.fix: Remove the tftp client unless a device workflow truly needs it.
